LLM_Translation: A language that exhibits specific typological characteristics is Igbo: it has a system of definite articles and indefinite articles, a fixed order of numeral and noun in noun phrases, and adnominal demonstratives follow nouns. It also has no discontinuous adnominal property words, and nominal conjunction and comitative are expressed by different elements. It distinguishes inclusive and exclusive, but has no gender distinction in independent third-person pronouns. It does not have a dual form for all person categories, and it has fewer than three distance contrasts in demonstratives, with no elevation or visible/non-visible distinction. It has no demonstrative classifiers, no non-phonological allomorphy in noun number markers, and no suppletive nouns for number. It has a fixed order of adnominal possessor and possessed noun, and its core adjectives do not behave like verbs in predicative position. It has no morphological cases for non-pronominal or pronominal core arguments, and no prepositions or postpositions. Verbs have prefixes and suffixes beyond core-argument indexing, but no infixation. It marks present tense and past tense morphologically, but not future tense. It has a perfective/imperfective distinction, and it can index the S argument with suffixes/enclitics but not with prefixes/proclitics. It can index the A argument with prefixes but not with suffixes/enclitics, and it does not index the P argument. It does not vary core-participant marking strategies by TAM or by verb classes or by person distinctions, and verbs do not have suppletive forms for participant person or number. It has no benefactive or instrumental applicative markers on verbs, and no passive or antipassive morphology on lexical verbs. It also does not have an inverse marker on verbs. It does have serial verb constructions and clause chaining, but no switch-reference or simultaneous/sequential clause distinction. It does have causatives formed by affixes/clitics, but not causatives involving an element grammaticalized from a verb meaning “to say”. Verbs are reduplicated, but nouns are not. It has no copula for predicate nominals and no existential verb. It has no posture-verb alternation based on locatum shape, and it has a small number of verb roots. It uses SV order in intransitive clauses and SVO order in transitive clauses, and the constituent order is the same in main and subordinate clauses. Clausal objects occur in the same position as nominal objects, and core-argument order is fixed. Standard negation cannot be marked clause-finally or clause-initially, and there is no difference between imperative and declarative negation constructions. Verbal predication is not marked by the same negator as locational, existential, and nominal predication. There is no morphological passive on lexical verbs, and no phonologically independent reflexive or reciprocal pronouns. It has no passive particle, no antipassive particle, and no overt agent in passive clauses. It has no ideophone class beyond sound, and polar interrogation cannot be marked by intonation only, by special word order, by clause-initial or clause-final particles, or by a V-not-V construction. It has no comparative construction with a “surpass/exceed” form, and no comparative standard marker with locational meaning, but it can express comparatives using two conjoined clauses. It has no bound or non-bound comparative degree markers. It has no interrogative verb for content interrogatives, and content interrogatives do not occur in situ. It has no count/mass distinction in interrogative quantifiers. It has no postnominal relative clauses, no prenominal relative clauses, no internally-headed relative clauses, no correlative relative clauses, and no non-adjacent relative clauses. It has a decimal numeral system, but no quinary numeral system.
